pullRequests.body:
Smoothness pass for low-end and high-end devices. Every change keeps existing features, audio output and UI identical. It only removes repeated or wasted work.

## Found → fixed

**Startup & playback**
- An idle ticker read of `player.isPlaying` (its value was never used) built ExoPlayer and its media cache on Main at launch. → Read removed.
- Diagnostics queried the system exit history and decoded tombstone/ANR traces in `attachBaseContext`, before the first frame. → Moved to a background thread. Logging and the crash handler still install first.
- The log writer formatted each record twice and flushed after every record. → One append and one flush per batch.

**Network**
- One feed refresh downloaded and parsed `FEmusic_home` 3–4 times (mixes, songs, shelves, taste feed). → Callers share the request already in flight.
- Autocomplete used a blocking `execute()`. A lookup cancelled by the next keystroke kept running and then tried the second endpoint. → Uses the shared cancellable call.
- Synced-video alignment audio was fetched in 1 MiB ranges, over the 512 KB googlevideo limit. → Uses `YOUTUBE_RANGE_BYTES`.

**Library & storage**
- Every playlist change queued its own full-library recovery JSON write. → Conflated writer. Each pass re-reads Room, so the newest state is still written.
- `getLikedSongs()` / `getLocalSongs()` decoded every playlist to return one row, on every like, local scan and search keystroke. → Single-row query. A failed read still falls back to the full path.
- Playlist JSON was decoded on Main when a screen called `getAll()`. → Decoded on `Dispatchers.Default`.
- The 8 s YouTube library refresh decoded every cached playlist file just to get a cover. → Disk is read only as the last fallback.

**UI**
- Five shared loaders (feed/shelf skeletons, preview shimmer, generation card, screen loader) ignored the visibility gate, so hidden tabs requested a frame every vsync. → `rememberAmbientFloat` holds them still while hidden.
- Canvas copied a TextureView frame on Main (`getBitmap`) for a callback no caller passes. → Dead capture path removed.
- Local Music and Downloads called `lowercase()` inside comparators (n·log n string copies per keystroke). → Keys computed once per item. Same stable order.
- Local Music refiltered albums, artists and folders on every keystroke, though only one tab shows. → Only the open tab is computed.

**Audio (bit-identical output)**
- Exclusive USB output allocated a new PCM array for every chunk. → Arrays are reused after the native write, which copies and releases them in-call.
- The DSD JNI bridge allocated vectors inside `GetPrimitiveArrayCritical`. → Per-thread scratch, sized before the critical section.

## Verification
- CI on this PR runs `:app:testDebugUnitTest` and `assembleRelease` (Kotlin + native).
- Not run on a device. Frame-time, startup and allocation gains are not measured.

### Summary
Resolves track matching precision issues when converting Spotify recommendation candidates to playable YouTube Music tracks. Previously, tracks with multiple artists (e.g. Offset feat. Travis Scott) or matching common titles could resolve to unrelated tracks because featured artists were not combined into the search query and the target track duration was omitted during candidate resolution.

### Technical Changes
- **`InnerTubeMusicApi` / `InnerTubeMusicApiStreamResolver`**:
  - Extended `findBestMatchOrNull` with an optional `expectedDurationMs: Long? = null` parameter forwarded to `findBestMatchImpl`.
  - Enables `TextMatch.isSevereDurationMismatch` to reject candidate tracks with > 30s runtime drift and applies a +300 affinity score bonus for close duration matches (±3s).
- **`RecommendationRepository`**:
  - In `spotifyTracks`: extracts `expectedDurationMs` from `candidate.duration_ms ?: candidate.durationMs` and passes it to `findBestMatchOrNull`.
  - Automatically appends featured artists (`<Primary> feat. <Secondary>`) when Spotify candidate tracks provide multiple artist entries and the title does not already contain a featuring clause.
  - In `relatedFor`: returns Spotify tracks when $\ge 3$ verified matches exist. When 1–2 tracks match, complements the queue up to `limit` with native YouTube Music related tracks (`relatedGraph.relatedFor`) with deduplication. Falls back completely to YouTube Music when 0 tracks match or when the Spotify endpoint is unreachable.
- **Unit Tests**:
  - Extended `RecommendationRepositoryTest` to verify duration forwarding, featured artist query generation, threshold queue sizing (direct vs complementary vs fallback), and deduplication.

### Verification
- Tested with Gradle unit test suite: `:app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.lastwave.app.data.recommend.*` (10/10 tests passed).

## Problem
Tapping **Add to playlist** on a song played from device storage didn't list the user's existing playlists. It opened an offline-only sheet that showed offline playlists or, if there were none, only asked to create a new one.

## Cause
`AddToPlaylistDialogHost` sent every device song (no `videoId`, local URL) to a separate offline sheet. Regular custom playlists do accept local files (`PlaylistRepository.addTrack` keeps them, and the host already hides YouTube playlists for local files), so the user's own playlists were hidden for no reason.

- Every song gets the same sheet. For a device song it lists **your playlists** plus **offline playlists** as a second section.

## Problem
A user reported the app freezing for 3–4 s on launch, plus stutter when the feed auto-refreshes.

On a CPH2649 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, release build), every cold start had 3 frames of 450–700 ms. Frame stats put all of that time before the frame starts (vsync → `HandleInputStart`), not in drawing. A scheduler trace shows the main thread running flat out for 439, 624 and 520 ms at those exact moments, in code that emits no trace sections. A method-sampling trace of the debuggable build attributes the work outside frames to `SettingsPreferences.settings` mapping (`map…emit` + `collect` + `Keys` init) and to BotGuard's WebView creation.

## Changes
1. **`SettingsPreferences.settings`**: this was a cold flow. Each of ~60 collectors, most on Main, re-ran the ~100-key mapping and the addons JSON parse on every write to the DataStore. It now maps once per change on `Dispatchers.Default`, skips unchanged values, and shares the latest one (`shareIn`, `replay = 1`). The type stays `Flow<MiscSettings>`, so callers are unchanged; `first()` and `drop(1)` behave as before.
2. **`MainShell` pager**: Statistics and Playlists were composed on the launch frame and started their own loads. They are now composed once the user first leaves the Feed, then kept composed as before, so a dock jump back to Feed still never rebuilds it.

## Measured
Change 2, non-debuggable bench build, OnePlus Pad, 5 cold starts each:

| | main-thread CPU (first 12 s) | frames ≥ 100 ms |
|---|---|---|
| main | 916 ms avg | 4.2 |
| change 2 | 744 ms avg (−19%) | 3.2 |

Change 1 compiles but has **not** been run on a device (local builds ran out of memory). Please check it on device before merging.

## Not covered
- **Player-open stutter.** On the CPH2649 every open has 2–4 frames of 30–45 ms while the app is still `verify`-compiled. After `cmd package compile -m speed-profile` there are 0 frames over 16 ms. So it comes from running without AOT after each sideloaded update, until Android's background dexopt applies the baseline profile. No code change here.
- **Return after a few minutes.** `FeedViewModel.onVisible()` refreshes after 90 s and the feed is rebuilt for each of 3–4 progressive updates. Unchanged; a repro on the CPH2649 showed one 53 ms frame.
- **Reported crashes.** No diagnostics file.

## Problem
`SENSITIVE_PREFERENCE_NAMES` keeps `lw_addon_url` out of exported backups, because addon URLs carry an access token (`/a/<token>/`). The multi-addon list that replaced it, `lw_http_addons_json`, holds the same URLs but was not in that set. Every exported backup therefore contained the user's addon tokens in clear, and anyone given the file could use those addons as that user.

## Fix
Add `lw_http_addons_json` to `SENSITIVE_PREFERENCE_NAMES`. One line.

As with `lw_addon_url`, restoring a new backup leaves the addon list empty, so the user adds their addons again. Older backups that still contain the list restore it as before.

## Problem
A user reported that a 10-song playlist doesn't stop after song 10 and starts over.

- **Repeat off:** when a song fails (unavailable, region-blocked, stream error), the skip path in `MusicPlayer` wrapped to `0 until failedIndex` and `nextQueueIndex` wrapped to `(0 until start)`, whatever the repeat mode. If the last song failed, the whole playlist played again. In shuffle mode the wrap could pick songs that had already played.
- **Repeat all + shuffle:** every round reused the same shuffle order, so the "loop" was the same sequence each time.

A normal end with repeat off was already correct: the player starts similar-songs radio (which skips every queued song) or stops.

## Fix
- The unavailable-skip wrap, and `nextQueueIndex(..., wrap = false)` on that path, now go past the end only on repeat-all. With repeat off, playback stops there. Manual next still wraps as before.
- On repeat-all + shuffle, a new shuffle order is dealt when playback wraps to the first song: both on ExoPlayer's own AUTO transition and on the STATE_ENDED fallback. The shuffle toggle uses the same new `reshuffleFrom()` helper.

2 files, +27/−9.

## Not verified
Not built or run on a device.

## What changed

**1. Video: clean frame after the controls time out** (`SyncedVideoPlayer.kt`)
"Choose video" and ✕ were drawn twice: once in the top bar and once more in two `AnimatedVisibility(visible = !controlsVisible)` blocks. The second copy appeared exactly when the bar hid. I deleted the duplicates, so all of them now fade with Now playing and quality. Nothing else in the video player changed.

**2. Home feed takes 10 s+ to load; "Not in the latest refresh" cards**
- **Cause of the slow load: #643 (`cfdd23dc`).** `FeedScreen` marked every synthetic section (`feedSectionsAwaitingData`) as pending while `lastUpdatedMillis == 0`, and `readyFeedSections` stopped at the first pending key. The repository's early `onUpdate`s (home shelves, familiar quick picks) were ignored, so everything under *My genres* stayed behind a spinner until the slowest fetch in `loadFeed` returned (discovery timeout, artist/album/Last.fm round-trips). Each section now renders as soon as it has data, in its configured order, as it did before #643.
- **The placeholder also came from #643.** `lastCompletedFeed` holds the raw final feed, and the `previous` fallbacks were removed from the repository. Any section that wasn't re-fetched therefore got a "Not in the latest refresh" overlay.
- **`4d724aa1` only hid that overlay:** `hasFreshFeedSection` was stubbed to `true` and `StableFeedSection` became a plain `Box`. It did not touch the slow load, and it left `FeedSectionOrderTest` / `FeedViewModelChipsAndPaginationTest` asserting values the stub can no longer return. CI does not run those feed tests, so this went unnoticed. This PR deletes the dead plumbing (helper, composable, androidTest, string ×3 locales) and inlines `isUnavailable = false`. Rendering is identical.

**3. Mixed card shapes in one shelf** (`FeedShelves.kt`)
`HomeShelfCard` picked a card variant per item. *Forgotten favorites* mixed a 16:9 video, a tall community-playlist card and square songs, and one community item sent the whole row to `CommunityDiscoverShelf`. This left blank space under the shorter cards. A row whose items need different variants now renders them all as square cards; podcast episodes keep their own card. Rows of a single variant are unchanged.

**4. Beat-synced fluid motion is opt-in again**
It shipped on by default. The default is now off in the settings model, the read fallback, the composable defaults and `FluidRhythmEngine.isEnabled`. The Settings toggle still turns it on, and anyone who turned it on themselves keeps it.

## Why

The beat-synced fluid work (`ddf78084` … `5fce7549`, pushed straight to `main`) changed the shared player background for **everyone**, including users with beat sync off:

- `5fce7549`: the blurred-cover fallback was always drawn under the fluid, so two different blurs mixed during fade-ins and track changes. Before, it showed only until the fluid appeared.
- `f699c983`: `rememberIsForeground()` replaced `rememberPlayerWindowActive()` (#574), so the background kept animating under the notification shade.
- `b34da217`: the graphics layer read `seconds` on every frame; the full-screen-art scrim was roughly halved for everyone.
- `8ec2d947`: three radial gradient layers were always drawn under the player as a guard against beat sync's own black-screen bug.
- `ddf78084` / `920fadef`: an `audiofx.Visualizer` was attached to **every** playback session at max capture rate, setting on or off.

## What changed

1. **`FluidArtworkBackground.kt` is back to its pre-`ddf78084` code byte for byte.** The only addition is a `fluidBeatSyncEnabled` switch that hands off to `BeatSyncFluidArtworkBackground`.
2. **`BeatSyncFluidBackground.kt`** holds the beat-sync background **unchanged**. Only the names that would clash are renamed, and it reuses the shared shader and `isFluidSupported()`. With the setting on, it renders exactly as before.
3. **`FullPlayer`**: the gradient layers and the lighter scrim apply only with beat sync on; otherwise the scrim is the original (including the 0.65 stop).
4. **`FluidRhythmEngine`**: the Visualizer is created when beat sync turns on and released when it turns off or the session ends. The PCM analyser was already gated on `isEnabled`.

Beat sync stays off by default (#666) and can be turned on in Settings.

- Not run on a device: neither the default look against a pre-`ddf78084` build nor beat sync on/off switching.

**1. Feed pages in more shelves while the rest of the feed loads** (`FeedViewModel`, `FeedScreen`)

Scrolling down in the first seconds hit the end of the list, and the next shelves appeared all at once later. Paging now starts as soon as the first shelves are on screen, as it did before #643.

pullRequests.body: ## Problem Analysis Currently, LastWave offers a single visual presentation for synced and unsung lyrics. Users cannot customize the visual depth, typography weight, or motion choreography of the lyrics screen—nor is there a visual progress indicator during instrumental intros and interlude gaps—without altering the existing default lyrics experience. ## Summary of Changes - **Lyrics Style System (`LyricsTheme.kt`, `LyricsBlur.kt`)**: - Introduced a declarative `LyricsStyle` enum (`DEFAULT`, `FLOW`, `HALO`) persisted via DataStore preferences, keeping LastWave's existing lyrics renderer 100% untouched as `DEFAULT`. - Added hardware-accelerated Gaussian depth blur (`Modifier.lyricsBlurEffect` via `RenderEffect` on Android 12+ with graceful alpha fallback on older versions), automatically clearing blur when the user manually scrolls. - **Flow Style (`LyricsStyle.FLOW`)**: - Implemented whole-line magnification (`1.0x` active line vs. `0.58x` inactive lines over `300ms`) with proportional vertical layout scaling so surrounding lines compactly frame the active verse without empty gaps. - Added `650` display weight, selective soft white bloom on long active words, subtle `1750ms` horizontal micro-wobble, and `3000ms` breathing scale pulse on active instrumental breaks. - **Halo Style (`LyricsStyle.HALO`)**: - Implemented heavy display typography (`FontWeight.ExtraBold` / `FontWeight.Bold`), 6-step progressive downward blur (`2px` to `9.5px`), lingering `900ms` dissolve on finished past lines, and smooth duration-coupled vertical word rise (`+3.dp` to `0.dp`) with zero bounce or glow. - **Karaoke Canvas & Scroll Choreography (`ModernLyricsKaraokeCanvas.kt`)**: - Driven strictly by LastWave's native playback clock, sync offset, and syllable timestamps for zero timing drift. - Mapped horizontal left-to-right white progress sweeps per word with midpoint gap boundaries (`clipLeft`/`clipRight` and `splitTop`/`splitBottom`) to eliminate vertical glyph slicing on bold overhangs and wrapped multi-line verses. - Added `600ms` pre-emptive scroll lookahead with `400ms` ease-in-out transitions anchored at `45%` viewport height for fluid line progression. - **Music-Note Instrumental Break Loader (`InstrumentalBreakItem.kt`)**: - Added a bottom-to-top filling music-note Canvas indicator for both opening instrumental intros (`0ms` to first vocal line) and mid-track interlude gaps. - **In-Player Lyrics Style Chooser**: - Added a **Lyrics style** sub-menu row in the upper section of the player's **Lyrics options** modal (above the **Text size** slider) opening an instant-tick selection dialog (`Default`, `Flow`, `Halo`) with real-time updates and no extra confirmation step. ## Screenshots | Lyrics Style Chooser | Flow Style | Halo Style | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | |

Release notes

Sourced from org.robolectric:robolectric's releases.

Robolectric 4.18 adds Linux arm64 support to the native runtime, supports native resources on SDK 36 and above, and contains many performance improvements and bug fixes.

If you have any issues, please file them here.

Breaking Changes

  • Support for SDK 23 has been removed. The minimum supported SDK is now 24, matching AndroidX (#11604).
  • The shadows-httpclient module has been removed. It was deprecated in 4.17, and org.apache.http is no longer instrumented (#11373, #11544).
  • @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used (#11498).
  • ShadowRemoteCallbackList has been removed, as the real RemoteCallbackList works without it (#11368).
  • HttpResponseCache.install() now also sets ResponseCache.getDefault(), as it does on a device (#11493).

Linux arm64 support

Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. No configuration is needed (#11625, #11633). As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

Other Highlights

  • Native resources (ResourcesMode.NATIVE) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36 (#11578).
  • Robolectric no longer prints the "restricted method in java.lang.System has been called" warnings on JDK 24+ (#11482).
  • The shadow annotation processor now supports KSP (#10996).

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6

    java-version: '25'

pullRequests.body:
## Problem Analysis

Currently, lowering the device media volume to zero during active playback leaves the track running silently in the background, draining battery and losing the listener's place in the song or queue. Additionally, attempting to start or resume playback while media volume is muted offers no feedback, and stepping up from `0` volume starts at a barely audible `1%` increment.

closes #625 

## Summary of Changes

* **System Media Volume Observer (`ZeroVolumePlaybackObserver.kt`)**:
  * Added an isolated observer monitoring `AudioManager.STREAM_MUSIC` volume and mute state via `ContentObserver` (`Settings.System.CONTENT_URI`) and `android.media.VOLUME_CHANGED_ACTION`.
  * **Auto-Pause (`> 0` → `0` / Mute):** Automatically pauses playback when `pauseOnZeroVolume` is enabled and media volume reaches `0` while playing, tracking `pausedByZeroVolume = true`.
  * **Smart Auto-Resume with 10% Volume Floor (`0` → `> 0`):** Automatically resumes playback when volume increases above `0` if and only if playback was paused by zero volume, raising `STREAM_MUSIC` to at least `10%` of `getStreamMaxVolume()` (`ceil(maxVolume * 0.10)`) when incremented from `0` while preserving higher manual slider jumps.
  * **Manual & External Reset:** Clears `pausedByZeroVolume` immediately on manual transport actions (pause, play, skip, seek) or external interruptions (audio focus loss, headphone disconnect) so manually paused tracks never resume unexpectedly.
  * **Muted Play Guard:** Blocks play/resume actions when volume is `0` and the preference is enabled, emitting a snackbar alert via `snackbarEvent`.
* **Player & Snackbar Integration (`MusicPlayer.kt`, `PlayerViewModel.kt`, `PlayerHost.kt`)**:
  * Registered `ZeroVolumePlaybackObserver` on player initialization and unregistered it in `release()`, distinguishing zero-volume auto-pause from manual or focus-driven pauses.
  * Collected `viewModel.snackbarEvent` inside `PlayerHost` using `MiniPlayerAwareSnackbarHost` so alerts clear the mini-player cleanly.
* **Settings Toggle & Search Indexing (`SettingsPreferences.kt`, `SettingsViewModel.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`, `SettingsSearchIndex.kt`, `strings.xml`)**:
  * Added `pauseOnZeroVolume: Boolean = false` (`lw_pause_on_zero_volume`) to DataStore preferences so existing default behavior remains untouched out of the box.
  * Added the **Pause Playback at Volume 0** toggle card inside **Audio & Playback → Audio & Streaming** (between **Stop Playback When Swiped Away** and **Download Synced Lyrics**) and registered `audio.pause_on_zero_volume` in settings search.
* **Unit Tests (`ZeroVolumePlaybackObserverTest.kt`)**:
  * Added unit tests covering `> 0` → `0` auto-pause, `0` → `> 0` auto-resume, `10%` minimum volume restoration, manual reset, muted stream detection, muted play blocking with snackbar emission, and pass-through behavior when disabled.

## Verification

* **Unit Tests (`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*ZeroVolume*'`)**: All unit tests passing.
* **Debug Build (`./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`)**: Built cleanly with zero compilation errors or warnings.
* **On-Device Hardware Verification**: Verified on physical Android hardware using the volume rocker, settings toggle, and transport controls.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the OriginOS music card lyrics (802b4d5). On a vivo phone, the lyrics showed on the music card in the notification shade, but often not on the Origin Island or the lock screen, and the card sometimes showed a different, worse version of the lyrics than LastWave's own lyrics screen. This change fixes both.

The same behaviour has been running on a vivo phone (OriginOS, `com.vivo.musicwidgetmix` 17.0.8.3) as a patch to LastWave 5.2.1, through several days of testing. This PR is that behaviour written into the app.

## What was wrong

1. **The island forgets the lyrics.** The island and the lock screen widget drop the lyrics whenever they are drawn again (the screen locks, the island collapses and expands), and the card never asks the app for them again. The card in the notification shade keeps its own copy, which is why lyrics showed there and not on the island. Resending every 25 s left the island empty for up to 25 s each time.
2. **The card's lyrics differed from the lyrics screen.** The service fetched lyrics as soon as the track changed, usually before the duration was known, and sent the provider's lines as they came. Some providers then returned another cut of the song (one stopped halfway through *Bohemian Rhapsody*; another left a 40 s gap). The lyrics screen waits for the duration, and sanitizes and re-times the lines.
3. **The lyrics restarted.** The lyrics screen publishes each provider's answer as it arrives (three versions within 5 s for one song). The card starts the lyrics over with every one it gets.

## Changes

- `OriginOsMusicCard.LYRICS_RESEND_INTERVAL_MS`: 25 s → 4 s.
- `OriginOsMusicCard.playerLyrics`: the lines the lyrics screen shows, published from `PlayerViewModel.publishLyrics` for synced lyrics, keyed by the track (`trackKeyOf`, the identity `mediaIdOf` already used).
- `publishOriginOsLyrics` now sends the lyrics screen's lines once they have not changed for 2 s (`PLAYER_LYRICS_SETTLE_MS`). Until then, or when no screen is open, it uses its own fetch.
- The service's own fetch (`fetchOriginOsLrc`) waits up to 8 s for the track's duration, as the lyrics screen does, and prepares the lines with `LyricsSanitizer.sanitize` and `LyricsRepository.normalizeLyricTiming`. Instrumental results are skipped.
- One new unit test for `trackKeyOf`.

## Testing

- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*OriginOsMusicCardTest'`: 12 tests pass (on `main` at b457952 with this change).
- **Not run on a device as this source change.** The same behaviour (4 s resend, preferring the lyrics screen's lines after they settle) was tested on the phone as a patch of LastWave 5.2.1.
- Known limitation, not fixable from the app: after LastWave is reinstalled or updated while the card still lists it as the current app, the card does not reconnect to `MusicPlaybackService` until the card is opened (or one of its buttons is pressed), and the island shows no lyrics until then. Apple Music behaves the same way on this phone.

Closes #685

## Problem Analysis

The system media notification currently surfaces a **Shuffle** action in the far-right control slot, requiring users to unlock their device and open the full player interface to toggle track or queue looping. Replacing this slot with a stateful **Repeat** control makes single-track and playlist looping directly accessible from the lock screen and notification shade without adding any settings clutter.

## Summary of Changes

* **Notification Custom Layout (`MediaSession` / `MusicService`)**:
  * Replaced the far-right **Shuffle** `CommandButton` in the Media3 notification custom layout with a stateful **Repeat** `CommandButton` bound to a dedicated `SessionCommand` (`ACTION_TOGGLE_REPEAT`).
  * Mapped button icons and accessibility labels dynamically across all three `Player.RepeatMode` states:
    * `REPEAT_MODE_OFF` → Standard repeat-off icon (`Repeat Off`)
    * `REPEAT_MODE_ALL` → Active repeat-all icon (`Repeat All`)
    * `REPEAT_MODE_ONE` → Repeat-one icon with badge (`Repeat One`)
* **Command Handling & Reactive State Synchronization**:
  * Handled `ACTION_TOGGLE_REPEAT` inside `MediaSession.Callback.onCustomCommand(...)` to cycle repeat modes cleanly (`OFF → ALL → ONE → OFF`).
  * Observed `Player.Listener.onRepeatModeChanged(repeatMode: Int)` to refresh `mediaSession.setCustomLayout(...)` in real time, keeping the notification icon synchronized whether toggled from the notification shade or inside the app.
* **Unit Tests (`NotificationRepeatActionTest.kt`)**:
  * Added unit tests verifying rightmost slot placement (confirming Shuffle is removed from the notification layout), full state cycling (`OFF → ALL → ONE → OFF`), and icon/label resolution per repeat mode.

## Verification

* **Unit Tests (`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*NotificationRepeat*'`)**: All unit tests passing.
* **Debug Build (`./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`)**: Built cleanly with zero compilation errors.
* **On-Device Verification**: Tested on physical Android hardware across the lock screen and notification shade, confirming live icon transitions and synchronization with the in-app player controls.

Fixes #708

### Cause
1. \FeedViewModel\ and \HomeScreen\ never populated user avatar from \YtConnection.photoUrl\ (it was only updated from Last.fm profile stats, leaving YouTube Music users with the default placeholder).
2. \ProfileAvatar\ called \ArtworkImage(name = 'profile', artist = 'avatar')\ which ran track artwork resolution instead of directly loading the avatar image.
3. Fallback used \Icons.Filled.AccountCircle\ inside a circular Surface and circular border Box, creating an unsightly nested-circle appearance.

### Solution
- \FeedViewModel\ now exposes YouTube user's \photoUrl\ and lazily fetches account info if missing.
- \HomeScreen\ receives \ytConnection.photoUrl\ from \MainShell\.
- \ProfileAvatar\ uses \SubcomposeAsyncImage\ with \CircleShape\ crop.
- Replaced \Icons.Filled.AccountCircle\ with \Icons.Filled.Person\ for fallbacks to remove the nested circle.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

AutoMix was a two-player volume fade: the analyzer read compressed packets as PCM (fake 120 BPM / 8B), the planner never saw the outgoing song, and the native mixer was disconnected. This rebuilds it end to end on the existing two-ExoPlayer standby.

```text
tick (25% / <90s left)
  analyze current outro + next intro      # MediaCodec via the player's cached, range-chunked source
    TrackAnalyzer                         # tempo/beat/bar grid, key, silence, ending, phrases, 3-band waveform
  TransitionPlanner
    beatmix   if both grids confident, tempo within 6% (half/double ok), user speed 1x
                cue on downbeats / phrase starts, 4-8-16 bars, shorter on key or vocal clash
    fade      else, shaped by the real ending (fade-out / cold / natural), dead air trimmed
    bypass    short tracks, podcasts, consecutive album tracks (gapless)
  cue standby at the cue point, then blend
    PhaseLock     live kick onsets on both decks (KickTap) -> seek + <=1.5% speed nudges
    DeckEqStage   incoming enters on mids, highs open, bass swaps on the middle downbeat
    MixCurve      bass owner stays at full level, summed gain capped
    hand-over at 50%, complete or interrupt
```

One owner for every interruption:

```diff
 seekTo / skip / queue edit / speed / Cast / error / release
   cancelCrossfade()
+    autoMix.endTransition()   # commit after hand-over, revert before it
```

UI: tapping the quality badge opens a centered studio popup that expands from the badge's bounds without stretching its contents. The popup is capped at 520 dp, uses compact track headers and low-resolution covers from the shared artwork resolver, and keeps the normal Signal Path outside the final-25-second / three-second completion window. A fixed blue/orange/cream spectrum, cyan/yellow level envelopes and green playhead stay readable with monochrome app themes. Both waveform lanes run at full visibility to the chart edges; the closest real endpoint magnitude continues across context outside the available audio, without changing the timeline. The real overlap is centered with exactly three seconds of context before and after it; the cursor continues to the far edge during UI-only post-roll.

When mix telemetry lacks waveform samples, a silent Media3 preview decoder captures real PCM around each cue using the player's existing byte cache, extractors, minting headers and bounded ranges. Cue windows begin preparing from the mini-player host before the popup is opened, persist through handover, and retry failed reads while the current plan remains active. PCM is cropped in media time after subtracting Media3's renderer offset; the decoder never acquires an audio output or audio focus. Source MIME and optional independent DRM sessions are retained. Both raw source waveforms remain visible independently of mix gain and EQ. The AutoMix/status labels are larger and bolder, and the original hue-cycling rainbow neon badge rim, inner glow, dark backdrop and fade timings from `57317616` are restored.

The only changes in MusicPlayer are exposing its existing cache and extractor factories to the UI; their implementations are unchanged. Playback decisions, cues, mix wiring, analysis storage and output routing remain unchanged.

```text
app/src/main/java/com/lastwave/app/playback/automix/
├── analysis/   PcmWindowDecoder, TrackAnalyzer, AcousticSignatureExtractor/Store (disk cache, versioned)
├── engine/     DualDeckTransportCoordinator, TransitionPlanner, DeckEqStage, KickTap, MixCurve
└── api/        telemetry + MixView
ui/player/automix/AutoMixDeckView.kt
```

Removed: disconnected native automix C++ (crossover/stretcher/LUFS), loop/spectral scaffolding, fake estimators, `LOOP_LOCKED`/`LOOP_DROP`, unused unit wrappers.

## Evidence

- **Before:** analysis returned 120 BPM / 8B for every song; `outgoingSignature = null`; seek after hand-over used outgoing timestamps; force-commit could swap back to the outgoing deck.
  **After:** new unit tests on synthetic audio with known answers, run in CI (`com.lastwave.app.playback.automix.*` added to `build.yml`):
  ```text
  TrackAnalyzerTest     124 bpm +-1%, downbeat +-30 ms, noise not trusted, key 8A/8B,
                        silence trimmed, fade-out/cold endings, phrase start at section change
  TransitionPlannerTest beatmix on downbeats, half-time, speed/tempo/vocal/key guards,
                        ending-shaped fades, manual length, phrase-aware cue, bypasses
  DeckEqStageTest       idle bit-exact, 50 Hz -15 dB / 1 kHz untouched, treble cut, restore to bit-exact
  KickTapTest           kicks found within 15 ms in playback time, grid offset median
  AutoMixRenderTest     renders transitions to WAV: every beat within 20 ms, no clipping,
                        no level dip > 4.5 dB (renders uploaded as CI artifact)
  ```
  The render test caught a real ~7 dB dip at the bass swap (blend cancellation + equal-power sag), fixed by the filter-sweep EQ and BASS_SWAP curve.
- Waveform/neon follow-up (`71aebe36`): source/call-site review and `git diff --check` passed. Added CI protocol tests for real PCM window cropping with renderer offsets, float stereo buffer consumption/averaging, and flush/seek reset. Existing AutoMix regression CI includes these tests. No local Gradle build was run. [GitHub verification](https://github.com/Clash-Projects/LastWave-Native/actions/runs/45006175187) passed compilation, all three new waveform capture tests, existing download/playback/AutoMix regressions, release APK creation and signature verification; the signed APK artifact is uploaded. On-device waveform verification remains pending. GitHub currently reports merge conflicts with main.
- Neon/waveform edge polish (`473e6014`): only two UI files changed; historical neon helper verified against `57317616`, spectral paths re-read and `git diff --check` passed. [GitHub verification](https://github.com/Clash-Projects/LastWave-Native/actions/runs/45012471905) passed compilation, regression tests, release APK creation and signature verification; the signed APK artifact is uploaded. No local Gradle build was run; device visual verification remains pending.
- On-device listening: not done yet.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the old fade. Analysis cache lives in `filesDir/automix` (versioned JSON, ignored on mismatch).

**Blast Radius:** playback

AutoMix is off by default; with it off, the only always-on changes are: `cancelCrossfade` calls `endTransition()` (no-op without a session), the sink's EQ/kick stages return immediately when idle (bit-exact), Jam state is forwarded, and the player listener ignores speed changes only while AutoMix owns a deck's tempo. With it on: standby is seeked to cue points, tempo is stretched up to 6% during beatmixes, and analysis reads the outro/intro of the current and next stream (bounded ranges, cached).
